record.original_question: Let (M, g) be a closed symmetric space of noncompact type and of higher rank.

evidence.quote: Let (M, g) be a closed symmetric space of noncompact type and of higher rank.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g_0)$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) locally symmetric Riemannian manifold of noncompact type whose universal cover, viewed as a globally symmetric space, has rank at least $2$. A complete Riemannian metric $g$ on $M$ is said to have no conjugate points if, for every geodesic $\gamma:\mathbb{R}\to M$ of $g$ and every nonzero Jacobi field $J$ along $\gamma$ vanishing at some time $t_0$, $J(t)\neq 0$ for all $t\neq t_0$. 

Prove or disprove: every Riemannian metric $g$ on $M$ with no conjugate points is homothetic to $g_0$, i.e. there exists a constant $c>0$ such that $g = c\, g_0$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a well-known conjecture attributed to Spatzier, generalizing the Burns–Spatzier higher rank rigidity theorem (which assumes nonpositive curvature) to the no-conjugate-points setting. Available surveys and recent works on higher rank rigidity discuss it as still open; partial results exist under additional hypotheses (e.g. nonpositive curvature, bounded asymptote, or structural assumptions), but a full proof in the no-conjugate-points generality has not been reported.

status_evidence.title: Open problems and questions about geodesics
status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture 7.2.3 (Spatzier): Let (M,g) be a closed symmetric space of non-compact type and of higher rank. Then the only metrics on M with no conjugate points are homothetic rescalings of g.
status_evidence.claim: States the conjecture as a listed open problem.

status_evidence.title: An Invitation to Rigidity Theory (R. J. Spatzier)
status_evidence.snippet: Burns and Spatzier proved that every compact irreducible Riemannian manifold with nonpositive curvature and higher rank is a locally symmetric space.
status_evidence.claim: The known higher rank rigidity result is in the nonpositive curvature setting; the no-conjugate-points version is the conjectural extension.
